title: Ecclesiastes 3
paragraphs: ¹ There is a time for everything, a season for every purpose under heaven: ² A time to be born and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot. ³ A time to kill and a time to heal; a time to tear down and a time to build. ⁴ A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance. ⁵ A time to scatter stones and a time to gather them; a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.

⁶ A time to search and a time to give up; a time to keep and a time to throw away. ⁷ A time to tear and a time to mend; a time to be silent and a time to speak. ⁸ A time to love and a time to hate; a time for war and a time for peace. ⁹ What does the worker gain from all their toil? ¹⁰ I have seen the burden God has laid on the human race.

¹¹ He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart — yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end. ¹² I know there is nothing better for people than to be happy and to do good while they live. ¹³ That each person may eat and drink and find satisfaction in all their toil — this is the gift of God. ¹⁴ I know that everything God does will endure forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God does this so that people will stand in awe before him. ¹⁵ Whatever exists now has existed before, and what is to come has been before; God calls the past to account.

¹⁶ And I saw something more under the sun: in the place of justice — wickedness was there; in the place of righteousness — wickedness was there as well. ¹⁷ I said to myself, "God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and every deed." ¹⁸ I also said to myself, "As for humans, God tests them so they may see that they are like the animals." ¹⁹ Surely the fate of human beings is like that of the animals — the same fate awaits them both: as one dies, so dies the other. All have the same breath; humans have no advantage over animals. Everything is meaningless. ²⁰ All go to the same place; all come from dust, and to dust all return.

²¹ Who knows if the human spirit rises upward and the animal spirit descends into the earth? ²² So I saw that there is nothing better for a person than to find joy in their work, since that is their lot. For who can bring them to see what will come after them?
